title: Family IDs man killed during police traffic stop
article: A man who was killed by police gunfire during a traffic stop in Brampton has been identified by his family as Jermaine Carby.

The 33-year-old man was known to police. He had a history of violence, drug trafficking and drug possession, police records show. Carby also faced a number of charges in connection with incidents that happened in Toronto and Vancouver over the past 14 years. Some of those charges include manslaughter in connection with the stabbing of a 50-year-old Vancouver man, and assault charges.

Carby's family says he was trying to turn his life around. He died in hospital after being shot during a police traffic stop in the Queen Street East and Kennedy Road area at approximately 10 p.m. Wednesday.

Const. Lilly Fitzpatrick previously said that an on-duty officer stopped a vehicle in that area. The officer then called for another unit. Shortly after that, she said the officer activated the emergency button on his portable radio. That typically occurs when an officer needs immediate assistance or is unable to access their portable radio. It is not known how many bullets were fired. Eyewitnesses said they heard approximately three to five gunshots ring out that night.
The Special Investigations Unit has launched a probe into the shooting. Meanwhile, a small memorial has been growing at the scene to honour Carby.
The SIU is an arm's length provincial agency that investigates police-related incidents involving death, serious injury and allegations of sexual assault.
